subject: Archaeology
title: The Titanic: Most Famous Wreck
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Titanic: Most Famous Wreck usable.

hook.text: The 'unsinkable' Titanic hit an iceberg on April 15, 1912, and sank in under three hours, killing 1,517 people.

buildup.text: The wreck lay undiscovered at 12,500 feet for 73 years. Robert Ballard found it in 1985 using deep-sea cameras.

discovery.text: The ship broke in two on the way down. The bow section is embedded 60 feet into the mud. The stern is shattered.

twist.text: Iron-eating bacteria are consuming the hull. Scientists estimate the wreck will be completely gone by 2030.

climax.text: In 2023, a submersible visiting the wreck imploded, killing five passengers. The Titanic still claims lives.

punchline.text: The Titanic is disappearing. Bacteria are finishing what the iceberg started.

quiz.question: What is happening to the Titanic wreck?
options: Treasure hunters are dismantling it piece by piece
Iron-eating bacteria are consuming the hull and may destroy it by 2030
Deep ocean currents are burying it deeper into the seabed

details.summary: RMS Titanic struck an iceberg on April 15, 1912, and sank in the North Atlantic, killing over 1,500 people. Found in 1985 at 3,800 meters depth by Robert Ballard, the wreck has been extensively documented, raising complex questions about preservation, salvage rights, and underwater heritage.
details.whyItMatters: The Titanic is the world's most famous shipwreck and a test case for deep-sea heritage protection. Debates over artifact recovery, commercial exploitation, and memorial sanctity continue to shape international underwater heritage law.
takeaways: Titanic sank in 1912 and was found at 3,800 meters depth in 1985
Robert Ballard located the wreck using deep-tow camera systems
The wreck has driven development of underwater heritage law

faq.question: Is the Titanic being preserved?
faq.answer: No — the wreck is actively deteriorating. Iron-eating bacteria are consuming the hull at an accelerating rate. Experts estimate the ship's recognizable structure may collapse within decades. Multiple expeditions have documented its condition, with each visit showing increased deterioration.

faq.question: Should artifacts be removed from the Titanic?
faq.answer: This remains fiercely debated. Salvors have recovered over 5,500 artifacts for museum display. Opponents argue the site is a mass grave that should be left undisturbed. International agreements now protect the wreck, but enforcement in international waters remains challenging.
